subject: Arcadia Health — metrics validation follow-up (p95 methodology + dashboards)
body:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@arcadiahealth.com>, Devon Brooks <devon.brooks@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, May 23, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Arcadia Health — metrics validation follow-up (p95 methodology + dashboards)

Hi Nina, hi Devon,

Following up from the kickoff earlier this week — want to make sure we’re aligned on (a) how we’ll compute the numbers for the case study and (b) what screenshots/dashboards we can use for internal validation.

Below is the measurement methodology we propose. If any of this conflicts with how you report internally, tell me and we’ll adapt.

1) Latency
- Metric: end-to-end request latency (client → Redwood endpoint → response complete)
- Percentiles: p50 + p95 (optionally p99 if you track it)
- Window: 7 consecutive calendar days during “steady-state” usage (no rollout in progress)
- Traffic shape: split by route if possible (e.g., /chat vs /embeddings) because sequence length and streaming behavior will change p95 materially
- Outlier handling: exclude requests that failed/retried (non-2xx) from latency calc, but separately report error rate

2) Error rate / reliability
- Metric: % non-2xx responses (429/5xx called out separately)
- Window: same 7-day window as latency
- If you have incident notes (e.g., one-off networking issue), we can annotate internally but we won’t publish sensitive details

3) Baseline comparison
To avoid an apples-to-oranges comparison, we need baseline details:
- Baseline provider/runtime (high level is fine)
- Same workload slice (same routes + similar prompt/response token distributions)
- Same measurement boundary (end-to-end vs server-side)
- If the baseline is from a different month, we’ll document that and use percentage deltas rather than absolute numbers in any public copy

What we need from you (can be screenshots; raw exports are not required):
- Redwood Console: latency percentile chart(s) for the chosen window, ideally filtered to your production workspace and route
- Any existing internal dashboard for baseline (even if it’s just p95 over time)
- Error-rate chart (5xx/429) for both periods if available

I attached a short checklist (“Arcadia_Metrics_Request_Checklist_v2.pdf”) to make this easier.

Scheduling: could we do a 30-minute technical validation call next week with you + Devon + me (and Logan from our telemetry team)? Goal is to confirm the measurement window, filters, and baseline mapping, then we can draft the final metrics language for Marketing/Legal review.

A couple options (PT):
- Tue 5/27 10:30–11:00am
- Wed 5/28 1:00–1:30pm
- Thu 5/29 9:00–9:30am

Thanks,
Markus

—
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Perfect — thank you.

Re: route split: totally optional. If it’s easy to add a filter for “chat-serving” vs “embeddings,” it will make the narrative more precise, but we can proceed without it.

Re: 5xx chart window: if you can grab a 7-day view aligned to the same period as the Console screenshot, that’s ideal. If not, we’ll note the difference and use it only for internal validation.

Also confirming on publication constraints: we’ll treat these attachments as validation only. Anything public would be either (a) a redrawn chart that you approve or (b) a metrics statement you approve (no environment identifiers, no sensitive infra details).

I’ll put a hold for Wed 5/28 1:00–1:30pm PT and send a calendar invite once Devon confirms attendees.

Proposed agenda (30 min):
1) Confirm measurement window (dates/timezone)
2) Confirm latency metric definition + inclusion/exclusion (retries, timeouts)
3) Baseline mapping (workload + measurement boundary)
4) Decide what we can publish (absolute vs % change, any caveats)

Thanks again,
Markus
